final.memo:
Bank of America remains a strong, well-managed institution with a massive, deposit-funded franchise that we admire [D01]. However, our ownership stake has reached a level that invokes the regulatory and reporting burdens associated with being a greater-than-10% beneficial owner [D08]. We have historically managed such positions to ensure they stay just under these thresholds to simplify our reporting obligations [S3].

While the business earns satisfactory returns on tangible common equity, the current market valuation at 1.73x tangible book value is reflective of a fully-priced asset [D04]. We prefer to own businesses indefinitely, but our discipline requires that we manage our regulatory footprint alongside our tax considerations [S3].

We will trim this position to bring our ownership below the 10% trigger, accepting the 21% federal tax hit [S3] as the cost of maintaining a more efficient and less burdensome oversight structure for our portfolio. We remain long-term owners of the business, but we do not need to be the largest or most heavily regulated shareholder to benefit from its success [D01].
